original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

actual_scope: On the selected PR1094 local program, screen the complete bounded family of disjoint fusions of consecutive same-column rank-1 climb pairs with exactly one intervening scalar event, allowing that scalar/frame schedule to change.
scope_change_reason: The generic decoder card is refined to a concrete retiming family in the pinned selected word. Unlike the active fixed-schedule frame and endpoint claims, this changes the local scalar schedule and paid rank profile. The complete zero-overhead profile is screened before any physical synthesis.
bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children account for 2,412 of the selected 5,586 local rank units. Combining two rank-1 children into one rank-2 child reduces the recursive moment per paid rank unit; the exact selected-word ceiling tests whether this bounded retiming family can clear the revision-3 5% mechanism gate.
stop_rule: Enumerate the source-pinned one-touch pairs in both directions, compute the exact maximum disjoint matching, and screen that complete profile at zero additional cost. Stop if the exact ceiling is below 1.05 times the selected ceiling upper endpoint.
evidence: Both directions contain 690 one-touch pairs and have identical candidate sets. A greedy matching and a separate path dynamic program agree that at most 674 can be used disjointly. The zero-extra-cost profile has exact ceiling bracket [0.001768911117731, 0.001768911117732], below the 5% target 0.00177455681454345; the least zero-overhead fusion count that passes is 720. The source-pinned verifier checks the archive and member hashes, source event data, baseline, matching, profile, ceiling intervals and adjacent 719/720 controls.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance for literature/overlap search, scope selection, exact matching analysis, implementation and packaging.

open_questions.question: Can pairs with two or more intervening scalar operations supply at least 720 disjoint rank-2 fusions without adding an expensive child?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The complete one-touch class cannot meet the 5% target, while another exact chronological class large enough to pass may still admit a useful retiming mechanism.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate consecutive same-column rank-1 pairs with exactly two intervening scalar events in both directions, intersect their identifiers, compute the maximum disjoint set, and screen the zero-overhead profile before synthesis.
open_questions.blocked_by: A physical construction must preserve both scalar dependencies, arbitrary dirty state, helper endpoints and restoration while fully charging any added frame or copy work.
